lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: These labels are much clearer than mine. At this rate, you can take over the whole café next week.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Are you serious? I can help with the boxes, but I don't want to manage the café.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: No, I was only kidding. I meant you're much better at organizing labels than I am.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I thought you meant you wanted me to cover more work. You asked me about the front counter last month, so it sounded possible.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Did it sound as if I had already made the decision for you?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Yes, and that was the part I wanted to check.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: I didn't realize it sounded like a real request. That came out wrong.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I don't mind a joke. I just need to know when a real responsibility is being offered.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: That's fair. I should've made the exaggeration clearer, or explained it immediately.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: And to be completely clear: I'm not asking you to manage anything. I'm only thanking you for fixing the labels.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Good. Then I'll finish this last box, and you can keep your café.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Now that one sounded like a joke.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It was—and I smiled before I said it.
